description: Woodwork teaches safe, skilled work with wood: shop safety and the Totin’ Chip, how lumber is grown, milled and graded, caring for and sharpening tools, building useful projects from your own drawings, and careers in woodworking.

safety.note: Wear eye and hearing protection and a dust mask, keep tools sharp, and use power tools only with adult supervision.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. Requirements 5 and 6 were not visible in the excerpts and are not outlined yet.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Safety
requirements.summary: Woodworking hazards, first aid, eye, hearing and dust protection, and the Totin’ Chip.

requirements.title: Wood
requirements.summary: How timber is grown and milled and how lumber is cured and graded, and collecting useful woods.

requirements.title: Tools
requirements.summary: Caring for and storing tools and sharpening cutting tools.

requirements.title: A woodworking project
requirements.summary: Building a useful project from your own drawings with hand tools.

requirements.title: Careers
requirements.summary: Talking with a cabinetmaker or finish carpenter about the trade.
